metadata.title: Above Avalon: How Apple Can Respond to Changing Search Behavior

content.text:
Hello everyone. Today's update will continue the discussion found in last Friday's article regarding how AI is impacting Google search.
How Apple Can Respond to Changing Search Behavior
Search’s future has been debated for years. We can go back to ChatGPT's early days when some of the chatbot’s initial users began to wonder what would happen to Google.
Over the past two to three years, a lot has changed. We have seen a cooling down of ChatGPT hype as other digital assistants entered the scene. Even the way we approach all-powerful assistants have in some ways come back to Earth. For the mass market, “AI” means getting better answers from Google and Siri. Search queries are longer, multimodal (voice and images), and more direct. Instead of seeking out a website that may or may not contain an answer to our question, we are getting used to receiving specific answers. While Google remains in a good position to provide those specific answers – the way Google can leverage YouTube videos to enhance search results is super intriguing - there is unknown found with how effective the companywill be in monetizing search not based on sponsored links. There is also a legitimate debate found with how Google can balance discovery, which is what advertisers are buying, with usefulness, which is what users are consuming.
While all of this plays itself out, we are also seeing some significant changes in how we are using our devices for reimagined search.
